title: SouthernSpear - Australian FPS Game like America's Army of Old in UE5.8
author: Remarkable_Potato861
selftext:
Hey all,

  
I'm currently using AI and free assets/animations/maps etc to re-create the classic America's Army game style in Unreal Engine 5.8 using Australian Military models, equipment and setting.

  
[https://theantipopau.github.io/southernspear-site/](https://theantipopau.github.io/southernspear-site/)

  
It's going well so far, and would love advice or opinions as I continue on this journey. I'm using Claude Code primarily, with plugins and custom skills to link into Unreal Engine. 



Some queries:  
Animations have bene difficult. Does anyone have recommendations for that?

Map layout is tricky, as some assets have no back to them, and placement is sporadic - again, any advice here?

I must applaud the AI for diving into this head first and creating some great starting blocks, importing free assets I've found, reverse engineering old mod packs that have long since been gathering dust on an external drive etc.

comments.author: IAmhowlshot
comments.body:
Ahah i remember that game. Played it a long time ago. Couldnt beat free shooter online at the time. 

For the parts youre struggling with, find references or things you want it to resemble or feel like. Claude loves having something to build towards to vs imagining it or following a written plan it created. 

Maybe find some maps you like in America's Army, or other games, like Battlefield. Start with that. Or have it do research and learn about creating battlefield maps, what makes them successful, which ones do people love the most and why. 

The old mod packs is an excellent idea. There's tons of assets floating around out there.

comments.author: fapfap_ahh
comments.body:
What I've found with animations is that if I have a model with the pieces that make it up, I can animate it myself.

Like yourself, I am using AI (Claude) to assist development. I've created a pipeline with a few scripts and a skill that lets me take an asset, break out it's parts, animate them how I want, implement it, GPU render it to test, then hand me a dev build for my own human playtest.
